subject: Clarify: default retention for prompts vs inference outputs
summary: Customer asked for explicit definitions of what Redwood stores by default (prompts, model outputs, embeddings), retention windows, deletion/purge capabilities, and redaction options. Internal product and privacy clarified hosted vs dedicated vs private defaults and next steps for a short attestation for procurement.
messages:
From: Amit Patel <amit.patel@finapp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify what Redwood stores by default (prompts vs outputs)

Evelyn —

Quick question from our security review: can you confirm exactly what Redwood stores by default for hosted API customers? Specifically:
- Are the raw prompts (user requests) and the model-generated outputs both retained as part of "request/response logs"?
- Do embeddings generated via your embeddings endpoint count as the same class of log?
- What are the default retention windows for these artifacts (prompts, outputs, embeddings, request metadata)?
- Do you ever use stored request/response data for improving models or analytics unless we opt in?

We're trying to reconcile your standard contract language with our procurement questionnaire — procurement wants a short clear answer and an attestation we can put in the contract.

Also: if we need a one-time purge or an ongoing shorter TTL, what are the supported options and SLA for confirming deletion?

Thanks,
Amit
Amit Patel

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify what Redwood stores by default (prompts vs outputs)

Evelyn / Marissa —

Quick technical breakdown below; feel free to copy-paste the bullets into a short note for the customer (I'll keep it concise):

- Hosted API (default):
  * Request/response logs: we persist the request payload (prompts) and the model-generated tokens (outputs) together as a request/response pair for operational and debugging purposes. Default retention window: 30 days.
  * Request metadata (IP, timestamp, route, model version): retained 30 days for telemetry and billing reconciliation.
  * Embeddings endpoint: embeddings are stored alongside the request/response record and follow the same 30-day default. If a customer explicitly flags data as sensitive, we have redaction tooling (see below).
  * Training/usage: Redwood does NOT use hosted API customer request/response data for model training or to improve public models unless the customer opts in through an explicit data-use agreement. We may use aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry for system performance improvements.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  * Default behavior: logs are persisted to the customer's dedicated storage (or a dedicated retention configuration) and retention is configurable by the customer. If the customer requests zero-retention, we can configure routing so logs are not retained beyond ephemeral caches.

- Private (VPC/on‑prem):
  * By default, logs remain entirely in the customer's control. Redwood's control plane only receives metadata required for orchestration; raw prompt/output content does not leave the customer VPC unless explicitly configured.

- Deletion / purge path:
  * Customers can request an ad-hoc purge via a support + compliance request. For hosted API data, deletion requests trigger: (1) removal from hot request/response store immediately, (2) cascading deletion from analytics and indices within 48–72 hours, and (3) confirmation email when purge completes.
  * Retention TTLs are enforceable via account settings for Dedicated customers; for Hosted we offer a shorter TTL as a configuration (e.g., 7, 14, 30 days) under contract.

- Redaction & PII handling:
  * Automatic redaction: we provide optional PII scrubbing at ingestion for common patterns (SSNs, credit cards, credentials).
  * Manual redaction: customers can submit redaction requests for specific records (we will provide a record id and deletion ticket).

- Caching / KV stores:
  * KV cache used for session continuation is ephemeral and not treated as persistent logs; it is evicted per cache policy and does not survive TTL unless explicitly persisted by customer configuration.

Let me know if you want a one-page attestation we can sign for procurement (I can draft it with Marissa).

—Rishi
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Amit Patel <amit.patel@finapp.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: default retention for prompts vs inference outputs

Amit —

Thanks for raising this. Below is a short customer-ready summary and the next steps. I attached a one-page retention table and our redaction playbook for reference.

Customer-ready bullets (copy/paste):
- By default, Redwood's hosted API retains request/response pairs (prompts and model outputs) and associated request metadata for 30 days. Embeddings generated by our embeddings endpoint follow the same default.
- Redwood does not use hosted API customer request/response content for model training or improvement unless you explicitly opt in; we may use aggregated telemetry for platform performance.
- Customers on Dedicated or Private deployments control retention settings; we can configure TTLs down to zero-retention for Dedicated, and all raw content remains in-customer for Private deployments.
- We offer ingestion-time PII redaction options and ad-hoc record-level purge. Hosted API purge requests typically complete with confirmation within 48–72 hours.

Next steps:
1) If FinApp needs, Evelyn and I can provide a short attestation statement (one paragraph) that you can include in your procurement docs.
2) If you prefer a shorter default TTL (e.g., 7 or 14 days) for hosted traffic under your account, we can put that into the SOW for Dedicated or apply a contractual configuration for hosted with an amendment.
3) I'll attach the redaction playbook and the retention table (see attachments).

Please confirm if the bullets are sufficient for procurement or if you need an explicit signed attestation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Compliance, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
